title: Apple TV+ Black Friday Deal: Stream for $6.99/Month – Limited Time Offer!
body:
Apple is rolling out a limited‑time Black Friday promotion that slashes the cost of its Apple TV+ streaming service to $6.99 per month for new subscribers and eligible returning customers. The offer, which begins today and runs through 8 p.m. Pacific Time on November 30, is available only to users in the United States and requires a qualifying Apple TV+ subscription plan. Those who take advantage of the deal will receive the reduced monthly price for the first year of service, after which the standard $9.99 rate will resume.

The promotion arrives at a pivotal moment for Apple’s media division. Apple TV+, launched in November 2019, has struggled to match the subscriber bases of entrenched rivals such as Netflix, Disney+, and Amazon Prime Video. While the platform has earned critical praise for original series like “Severance” and “The Morning Show,” its growth has been modest, prompting the company to experiment with pricing incentives and bundled offerings. By positioning the Black Friday discount as a “first‑year” rate, Apple hopes to lower the barrier to entry for budget‑conscious consumers who are already inundated with holiday‑season streaming deals.

Industry analysts see the timing as strategic. The holiday shopping period traditionally sees a surge in streaming service trials, as families look for new content to occupy winter evenings and gift subscriptions to friends and relatives. A $3‑per‑month discount represents roughly a 30 percent reduction, making Apple TV+ one of the most competitively priced premium services on the market. “Apple is leveraging the Black Friday hype to expand its footprint in a crowded space,” said Maya Patel, senior analyst at TechInsights. “If they can convert a significant portion of these trial users into long‑term subscribers, the revenue impact could be substantial, especially when combined with the ecosystem lock‑in that Apple devices provide.”

The deal also underscores Apple’s broader strategy of bundling services to increase customer loyalty. The company’s Apple One subscription bundle, which combines Apple TV+, Apple Music, iCloud storage, and other services, has already shown promising uptake. By offering a low‑cost entry point to Apple TV+, Apple may encourage users to eventually adopt the larger bundle, thereby boosting average revenue per user (ARPU). Moreover, the promotion could serve as a catalyst for content investment; a larger subscriber base strengthens Apple’s negotiating position with talent and production studios, potentially leading to higher‑budget original programming in the coming years.

Consumers should note the eligibility criteria. The discounted rate applies only to new Apple TV+ accounts or to existing accounts that have been inactive for at least six months. Users must sign up through the Apple TV app or the Apple website and will be billed at the promotional price for twelve consecutive months. After the introductory period, the subscription automatically renews at the regular $9.99 monthly fee unless cancelled. Apple has emphasized that there are no hidden fees or additional commitments beyond the standard service terms.

Looking ahead, Apple’s Black Friday offer could set a precedent for future pricing experiments across its services portfolio. If the promotion drives a measurable uptick in subscriber numbers and retention, the tech giant may replicate similar discounts for Apple Music, Apple Arcade, or even its fitness offerings. As the streaming wars intensify, price elasticity will remain a critical lever for platforms seeking to differentiate themselves. For now, the $6.99‑per‑month Apple TV+ deal gives shoppers a low‑risk opportunity to test the service’s growing library of original shows, movies, and exclusive sports content—potentially reshaping the competitive landscape as the holiday season unfolds.
